| A.05.02. | Frequency variation capability | NaN |
| NaN | (a) BESS shall be capable of delivering the declared active and reactive power outputs within the system Frequency variations, specified in this specification. Additionally, the PCS AC-side current of the BESS shall be capable of operating continuously at 110% of the rated current, sustain 120% of the rated current for ≥2 minutes, and preferably support short-term overloads of 150% rated current for 10 seconds. | comply |
| NaN | (b) Active and reactive power capability (±10 MW/ ±3 MVAr) of the BESS must be available for frequency range between 47 Hz to 52 Hz for at least for time related clause in A.05.04. ( consider real and reactive power loss transformer when calculating the BESS rating at POC. ) | comply |
| NaN | (d) The supplied active power shall be delivered to the network based on the nominated frequency droop settings and deadband settings. | comply |
| NaN | (e) BESS shall be protected against frequency excursion outside the frequency range specified in clause in A.05.04. and able to disconnect from the system if the extreme frequency could risk to the BESS performance and reliability. | comply |

| A.05.03. | Frequency support capability (refer figure A.05.03 in next sheet) | NaN |
| NaN | (a) The BESS must be capable of responding independently on a configurable droop curve in response to frequency deviations, without receiving external control signals from CEB. | comply |
| NaN | (b) Droop setting shall be able to set between 1% to 9% as per the CEB discretion. If CEB did not disclose any Droop value, then it shall be set at 4%. | comply |
| NaN | (c) During a sudden frequency drop BESS shall mimic an inertia response of a synchronous machine through its grid forming control system. | NaN | (f) No frequency regulation limit shall be set in principle, but if necessary, the limit shall be ≥20% Pn | comply |

| A.05.09. | Response to disturbances following contingency events | NaN |
| NaN | (a) BESS must remain in continuous uninterrupted operation for any disturbance caused by: \ni. a credible contingency event \nii. a three-phase fault in a transmission system cleared by all relevant primary protection systems (250 millisecond) \niii. a two phase to ground, phase to phase or phase to ground fault in a transmission system cleared in: \n a. the longest time expected to be taken for a relevant breaker fail protection system to clear the fault; or \n b. if a protection system referred to in subparagraph (a) is not installed, the greater of the time specified by CEB (or if none is specified, 550 milliseconds) and the longest time expected to be taken for all relevant primary protection systems to clear the fault; or \niv. a three phase, two phase to ground, phase to phase or phase to ground fault in a distribution network cleared in: \n a. the longest time expected to be taken for the breaker fail protection system to clear the fault; or \n b. if a protection system specified by CEB, the greater of 1000 milliseconds and the longest time expected to be taken for all relevant primary protection systems to clear the fault, provided that the event is not one that would disconnect the production unit from the power system by removing network elements from service. | comply |
| NaN | (b) BESS and each of its production units must remain in continuous uninterrupted operation for a series of up to 6 disturbances within any five minute period caused by any combination of the events described in paragraph (c) where: \n | comply |
| NaN | i. up to four of the disturbances (two LLLG faults, one LL and one LG fault) cause the voltage at the connection point to drop below 50% of normal voltage \nii. up to one disturbance is cleared by a breaker fail protection system or similar back-up protection system \niii. up to one disturbance causes the voltage at the connection point to vary within the ranges under clause A.05.08. . \niv. provided that none of the events would result in: \n a. the islanding of the generating system or integrated resource system or cause a material reduction in power transfer capability by removing network elements from service \n b. the cumulative time that voltage at the connection point is lower than 90% of normal voltage exceeding 1,800 milliseconds within any five-minute period \n c. the time integral, within any five-minute period, of the difference between 90% of normal voltage and the voltage at the connection point when the voltage at the connection point is lower than 90% of normal voltage exceeding 1 pu second. | comply |
| NaN | (c) BESS shall provide Inertia support during a fault \ni. The BESS shall provide a synthetic inertia support in response to a fault that mimics an inertia response of a synchronous generator. The maximum inertia time constant of the grid-forming electrochemical energy storage system shall be no less than 20 seconds, with an inertia response activation time ≤5 ms. The system shall allow flexible adjustment based on grid requirements. \nii. This synthetic inertia response shall be configured by the NSO as part of the design of the Facility for the purpose of network stability, and subject to approval by NSO. | comply |
| A.05.10. | Reactive current injection and active power recovery during the fault (refer figure A.05.10 in next sheet) | NaN |
| NaN | (a) Subject to any changed power system conditions or energy source availability beyond the BESS reasonable control, BESS respect of the types of faults described in subparagraphs clause A.05.09. must have BESS capable of supplying to or absorbing reactive current from the network: \n\ni. to assist the maintenance of power system voltages during the fault: \n a. BESS inverter shall inject reactive current during the fault (within their capability) based on the amount of remaining system voltage. Amount of reactive current during the contingency shall be equal to 2% for every 1% drop in voltage at the POC as a default value. Further, the BESS unit shall be capable of providing reactive current of x% per 1% drop in voltage at POC where x% shall be set between 1% to 6%. \n b. Additional reactive current injection during fault shall be in addition to the steady state reactive current given at that time by the BESS. \n c. during the disturbance and maintained until connection point voltage recovers to between 90% and 110% of normal voltage, or such other range agreed with the CEB; and \n\nii. from 100 milliseconds after clearance of the fault, active power shall recover to at least 95% of the level existing just prior to the fault. | comply |
| NaN | (b) CEB may request the contribution of positive, negative and zero sequence currents depending on the requirements of fault detection near the POC. \n | comply |
| NaN | (c) Allowable activation delays are between 20ms - 40ms (in order for ac protection systems to detect faults without undue delays) and provide or absorb the required reactive current within 70 milliseconds | comply |
| NaN | NaN | NaN |
| A.05.11. | Quality of electricity generated (harmonic, flicker and voltage unbalance) | NaN |
| NaN | (a) The BESS shall ensure that when connected to CEB network, it must not produce level of distortion or fluctuation of the supply voltage at the connection point: \ni. rapid voltage changes greater than 3% of the nominal voltage during the normal operation \nii. harmonic voltage distortion greater than the emission limits allocated by the CEB in accordance to 3.17.2.5 of Grid Connection Code. \n a. harmonic analysis shall consider harmonic order 2 – 50 \niii. voltage unbalance greater than the limits allocated by the CEB in accordance with IEC 60034-1. \niv. voltage flicker greater than the limits allocated by CEB, i.e., Pst = 0.35 and Plt = 0.25. \n | comply |
| NaN | (b) The design of the harmonic mitigation measures (including filters if required) shall be demonstrated through a harmonic analysis study. \n | comply |
| NaN | (c) Measurement and evaluation of respective emissions shall be carried out in accordance with IEC 61000-3-6. Measurement and evaluation reports shall be prepared in accordance with IEC 61000-3-6 and IEC 61000-3-7. | comply |

| A.05.14. | Voltage, reactive power and power factor control modes | NaN |
| NaN | (a) The BESS shall be able to provide automatic control at the POC over the entire operating range of the BESS, without causing system instability. Control modes include: \ni. Voltage control \nii. Voltage droop control \niii. Reactive power control \niv. Power factor control \n | comply |
| NaN | (b) The BESS shall be capable of contributing to voltage or voltage droop control at the POC utilizing its capabilities, while respecting reactive power capability and reactive power exchange with the AC network, in accordance with the following control characteristics: \ni. Voltage set-point at the connection point shall be capable of being specified within the range (0.9 pu-1.1 pu), either continuously or in steps. \nii. It shall be possible to operate voltage control with or without a dead band around the setpoint. The dead band shall be adjustable and agreed with CEB. \niii. Voltage droop control mode shall include the capability to change reactive power output based on a combination of a modified voltage set-point and an additional instructed reactive power component (i.e. voltage-reactive power droop). \nThe slope (i.e. voltage droop) shall be adjustable in the range (typically 2% -12%). | comply |
| NaN | \n(c) The BESS shall be capable of operating at a designated reactive power value specified by the CEB as long as the same is \nwithin the reactive power capability of the BESS. | comply |
| NaN | (d) The BESS shall be capable of controlling the power factor to a target at the POC, while respecting Reactive Power Capability and Reactive Power Exchange with the network. | comply |
| NaN | NaN | NaN |
| A.05.15. | Set point response | NaN |
| NaN | (a) The BESS inverter must be able to respond independently to separate command set points from National System Control Centre (NSCC) for the following performance characteristics under normal operating conditions: \ni. MW \nii. MVAr \niii. power factor \niv. voltage \n\n | comply |
| NaN | (b) Set point response shall be by bias of the relevant droop curve and grid support functionality shall be maintained, within the active and reactive power capability limits of the BESS. | comply |
| NaN | (c) The behavior of the relevant performance characteristic following receipt of a set point command at the Facility SCADA, subject to any pre-set ramp rate limitations, and limitations on the active and reactive power capability limits of the BESS, shall be as follows: \ni. Set point response must commence within 50 ms. \nii. Commanded set point value must be achieved within 300 ms \niii. Overshoot of the commanded set point value shall not exceed 10% of the value of the change in set point value. \niv. Settling time, to within 1% of full-scale output for the relevant performance characteristic, must be achieved within 400 ms. \nv. BESS shall automatically notify NSCC when its state of charge moves outside the normal operating state of charge limits as described in Functional Specifications and reduce the active power set point to zero in a manner pre-agreed with CEB. | comply |
| NaN | NaN | NaN |
| A.05.16. | Priority to Active or Reactive power contribution | NaN |
| NaN | (a) The BESS shall be capable of operating in the active or reactive power priority modes, as requested by CEB, while meeting continuous operating rating and short-term overload ratings. This includes utilizing the full rating (continuous and short-term overload) of the inverter current capability and operating in zero active power transfer. Taking into account the capabilities of the BESS, CEB may inform on case by case basis whether active power contribution or reactive power contribution has the priority during low or high voltage operation. \n | comply |

| A.05.17. | Control interaction with other generating devices | NaN |
| NaN | (a) Control Interaction is a specific issue that can impact the coordinated operation of Power Electronic devices in a local area. Control systems of dynamic devices can interact in an undesirable manner resulting in unstable or poorly damped oscillations following system disturbances such as fault recovery. \n\n\n\n\n\n\n | comply |
| NaN | (b) The BESS shall design the equipment to avoid such undesirable interactions, and the acceptable operation demonstrated through interconnection studies. | comply |
| NaN | (c) The BESS shall be capable of contributing to the damping of power oscillations in theconnected AC Transmission system. The Project Company shall require to provide all required data control system models including parameters for of any small signal modulation controls such as power oscillation damping (POD) controls, or sub-synchronous oscillation damping controls. | comply |
| NaN | (d) The grid-forming BESS shall have autonomous damping suppression functionality. When low-frequency oscillations (0.2 Hz–2.5 Hz) occur, the system shall suppress oscillations, with active power variation limited to 10%– 30% Pn. | comply |
| NaN | (e) The BESS shall be capable to inject or absorb active phase jump power into the system immediately due to the change of phase angle in the event of disturbance or failure of the system | comply |
| NaN | (f)Regarding the sub-synchronous torsional interaction (SSTI) damping control, the BESS shall be capable of contributing to electrical damping at torsional oscillation frequencies. The SSTI studies shall be undertaken by the NSO. The studies shall identify the conditions, if any, where SSTI exists and propose any necessary mitigation measures. | comply |
| NaN | (g) The BESS shall be capable of finding stable operation points with a minimum change in active power flow and voltage level, during and after any planned or unplanned change in the BESS or AC Transmission System to which it is connected. | comply |
| NaN | (h) The grid-forming BESS shall receive and respond to AGC (Automatic Generation Control) commands from the grid dispatch, with a regulation range of -100% to +100% Pn and steady-state active power deviation ≤2% Pn. It shall also receive and respond to AVC (Automatic Voltage Control) commands, with steady-state reactive power deviation ≤2% Pn. | comply |
| NaN | (i) The BESS shall support both grid-following and grid-forming control modes, enabling online switching between the two. | comply |
| NaN | (j) The grid-following mode shall operate stably under a minimum short-circuit ratio (SCR) of 1.2, while the grid-forming mode shall operate stably under a minimum SCR of 1.0. | comply |

| A.05.18. | Fault current | NaN |
| NaN | (a) the contribution of the BESS to the fault current on the connecting network through its connection point must not exceed the contribution level that will ensure that the total fault current can be safely interrupted by the circuit breakers of the connecting network and safely carried by the connecting network for the duration of the applicable breaker \nfail protection system fault clearance times, as specified for the relevant connection point by the CEB \n | comply |
| NaN | (b) BESS connected plant must be capable of withstanding fault current through the connection point up to the higher of: \ni. the level specified by CEB as per the clause A.04. \nii. the highest level of current at the connection point that can be safely interrupted by the circuit breakers of the connecting network and safely carried by the connecting network for the duration of the applicable breaker fail protection system fault clearance times, as specified by the CEB.\niii. circuit breaker provided to isolate a generating unit, generating system, bidirectional unit or integrated resource system from the network must be capable of breaking, without damage or restrike, the maximum fault currents that could reasonably be expected to flow through the circuit breaker for any fault in the network or in the generating unit, generating system, bidirectional unit or integrated resource system, as specified in the connection agreement. | comply |
| NaN | NaN | NaN |
| A.05.19. | Loss of communications | NaN |
| NaN | (a) In the event of loss of communications, the set point response of the BESS shall automatically revert to a state as agreed with CEB during design of the Facility. \n | comply |
| NaN | (b) Upon restoration of communications, the BESS plant shall not automatically restore operations but shall assess and issue ready status. Restart of operations shall only be commenced following instruction from CEB. | comply |
| NaN | NaN | NaN |
| A.05.20. | Safe shutdown | NaN |
| NaN | (a) In the event network fault that leads to power system conditions outside the requirements of this specification, the BESS must automatically execute a safe and controlled shutdown. \n\n | comply |
| NaN | (b) Upon restoration of standard operating conditions, the BESS plant shall not automatically restore operations but shall assess and issue ready status. Restart of operations shall only be commenced following instruction from CEB. | comply |
| NaN | (c) Subject to the limits of the backup power supply of the Facility, communications and essential functions shall remain operational throughout a safe shutdown event. | comply |
| NaN | NaN | NaN |
| A.05.21. | Protection from power system disturbances | NaN |
| NaN | (a) BESS to be automatically disconnected from the power system in response to abnormal conditions arising from the power system, the relevant protection system or control system must not disconnect the BESS for: \ni. conditions for which it must remain in continuous uninterrupted operation or \nii. conditions it must withstand under the Grid Connection Code; and \niii. a relevant system (as defined in paragraph (a)i connected to a transmission system must have facilities to automatically and rapidly reduce its generation: \n\n\n | comply |
| NaN | (b) CEB may require the BESS to be automatically disconnected by a local or remote-control scheme whenever the part of the network to which it is connected has been disconnected from the national grid, forming an island that supplies load. | comply |
| NaN | (c) Not withstanding clauses in Grid Connection Code or in this schedule, BESS may be automatically disconnected from the power system under any of the following conditions: \n a. in accordance with an ancillary services agreement between the BESS and CEB \n b. where a source of load that is not part of the BESS has the same connection point as the generating system and CEB agree that the disconnection would in effect be under-frequency load shedding \n c. where the generating system or integrated resource system is automatically disconnected under, Protection systems that impact on power system security or by an emergency frequency control scheme \n d. where the generating system or integrated resource system is automatically disconnected under Protection to trip plant for unstable operation; or \n e. in accordance with an agreement between the Project Company and CEB (including an agreement in relation to an emergency control scheme) to provide a service that CEB agrees is necessary to maintain or restore power system security in the event of a specified contingency event. | comply |
| NaN | NaN | NaN |
| A.05.22. | Data and information exchange between BESS and the System Control | NaN |
| NaN | (a) Exchanged Information \ni. Regarding instrumentation for the operation, the BESS module shall be equipped with an automatic controller capable of receiving instructions from the CEB system control. This automatic controller shall be capable of operating the units of the BESS module in a coordinated way. | comply |
| NaN | iii. The BESS controller shall be able to receive the following signals and commands from CEB based on communication with CEB. CEB shall specify the variable type and quality requirements of the supplied signals. \na. Start-up command \nb. Active power order set-point\nc. Frequency sensitive mode settings \nd. Reactive power, voltage, or similar set-points \ne. Reactive power control mode \nf. Power oscillation damping (POD) control settings, if applicable \ng. Synthetic inertia, if applicable \nh. Normal and emergency blocking command \ni. Ramp blocking command \nj. Remedial Action Schemes status and settings \nk. Active power flow direction command, if applicable \nl. Fast active power reversal command, if applicable \nm. Redundancy reductions and auxiliary power single source status \nn. Other project-specific set-points and commands, as specified by CEB. | comply |
| NaN | v. BESS EMS has the capability to record events where grid support services provided by the BESS and send the same data to NSO periodically. | comply |
| NaN | (b)The developer of the BESS shall install Grid Code Compliance Monitoring system with following features at the point of Common coupling to ensure that the installed BESS operates in accordance with the Grid Code. The developer \nshould integrate Grid Code Compliance Monitoring system to NSO's central monitoring infrastructure using standardized communication protocols. 3 and should provide comprehensive training for NSO personnel on system \noperation and data interpretation. Further, the developer shall establish a preventive maintenance program to ensure continuous system reliability. \ni. Real-time electrical parameter measurement: The device shall provides continuous monitoring of active power, reactive power, voltage, and frequency with high precision measurement capabilities. \nii. Power quality monitoring: The device shall be capable of analyzing power quality including harmonic distortion measurement up to the 100th order, voltage unbalance detection, and flicker monitoring. iii. Fault ride-through monitoring: The device shall detect voltage sag events and validates compliance with low voltage ride-through (LVRT) requirements\niv. Communication and control integration: The device shall support IEC 60870-5-104/101 protocols for seamless integration with NSO's SCADA systems \nv. Data storage and reporting: High-resolution data logging and automated compliance reporting capabilities. | comply |
| A.05.24. | Testing, monitoring and compliance review | NaN |
| NaN | (a) Testing and compliance \ni. The BESS shall be designed and tested to meet the requirements of the CEB operational requirements, performance studies and any Interconnection Agreements. Sufficient monitoring shall be provided to CEB to determine that the BESS complies with those performance requirements.\n | comply |
| NaN | (e) The BESS shall include any additional monitoring and recording required for the purpose of completing grid connection testing in the scope of supply. | comply |
